flags.estimate: {kind:'fullCharge'} — every charged pull (SR, chargeFrames 60 ⇒ ~1 pull/charge cycle)
flags.reasoning: The kit gates on Full Charge being MAINTAINED for ≥1 sec after reaching full charge. The engine releases charge weapons exactly at full charge, so no hold state exists; `fullCharge` is the closest primitive and fires on every charged pull. Against a player who holds, this is exact; against one who releases immediately, it over-fires. Since both effects are 40s windows on a ~1-2s cadence, uptime saturates either way — the error is confined to the first seconds of the fight.
flags.recipe: Focus recording: time the Pierce-icon appearance relative to the first shot. If the buff icon appears ~1s AFTER the first full charge rather than on release, the hold is real and the block needs a block-level delaySec ~1 (or an interval stand-in) instead.

flags.estimate: Window 35s, max-extended per own burst cast ⇒ with cd 40s the lapse fires at most once late in a 180s fight; expected ZERO firings in graded comps
flags.reasoning: The kit gives no activation event for 'High Tension is removed' other than its own expiry, and `selfStatusEnd` requires a `selfStatus` effect to arm it. Pairing the burst's named buff with a same-named 35s selfStatus is the only way to express the kit's penalty loop. Whether the game ALSO removes High Tension on some other condition (stack consumption, overwrite by another Tension source) is unknown; if it does, the ATK▼/stun pair would fire far more often and this baseline under-credits the penalty.
flags.recipe: Record a fight where the unit stops bursting for >35s: confirm (a) an ATK▼ popup on all allies, (b) a self-stun immediately after, (c) the 20s durations. Then confirm the inverse — burst every rotation and verify the penalty NEVER appears.

flags.estimate: 3 stacks, +1 per own burst cast; steady state 3 from the 3rd rotation on (time-average over a 180s fight ≈ 2.5 stacks ⇒ ~37% of the 45% ceiling-equivalent)
flags.reasoning: The kit states the cap but not the accrual rule. One-stack-per-cast is the default reading for a burst-applied stacking buff, and the 35s duration exceeds the 40s cooldown only marginally — so whether stacks SURVIVE to the next cast is itself uncertain (35s duration vs 40s cd suggests a 5s gap where a stack could lapse, which would pin the kit at 1 stack forever unless FB cadence is faster than cd). No rampSec authored: per-cast stacking already ramps, and layering rampSec on top would double-haircut.
flags.recipe: Popup/icon read across three consecutive bursts: count the stack pips on the ally buff icon at each cast. Critically, check the pip count IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the 2nd and 3rd cast — if it has dropped to 0, the 35s window genuinely lapses under a 40s cooldown and the buff never exceeds 1 stack.

flags.reasoning: A team-wide ATK ▼ scaled off the caster's ATK has no dedicated debuff StatKey; a negative casterAtkPct is the arithmetic equivalent on the flat-ATK path. The derived negative will not match index 9 of the level table, hence the [10] anchor. UNVERIFIED that the engine accepts a negative flat-ATK contribution without clamping at 0.
flags.recipe: Harness: force the lapse (patch the selfStatus durationSec down via withPatchedOverride), capture buffApply events with stat 'casterAtkPct', and assert the emitted value is negative and that the target's effectiveAtk actually drops by (10/100)×caster.staticAtk.

flags.estimate: stun durationSec 20 — zero shots fired for 20s, burst chain unaffected
flags.reasoning: Per the schema a stun blocks firing/charging/reloading but not bursting. For a Supporter this costs little damage directly, but it also stops the skill1 `fullCharge` trigger, so Pierce + Pierce Damage ▲60% lapse 40s after the last charge during a long stun — a second-order loss the kit text does not spell out.
flags.recipe: Same forced-lapse harness run: count shot events in the 20s after the lapse frame (expect 0) and confirm a burstCast still occurs inside the window if the gauge fills.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑: datamine cadence fields are known-unreliable, and here they set how often the skill1 pierce window refreshes and how often full charges land. A wrong charge time changes trigger frequency, not magnitudes, so the 40s windows absorb most of the error.
flags.recipe: Frame-count one magazine (6 rounds) of unbuffed fire from a focus recording: derive pulls/s and reload frames, compare against 60/151.
